solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Choosing awfully doting Pa?

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters of doting Pa are jumbled

explanation.surface: A doting father makes a poor job of picking something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' signals the anagram of DOTING PA.
explanation.definitionFit: Adopting a plan or name is selecting it, a direct synonym of choosing.

clue.text: Injury from run in European country

indicators.note: in places the run letter inside the name of the country

parts.note: Spain is a European country
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone hurts themselves while running on holiday in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprain is a type of injury, a twisted ligament in a joint.

clue.text: Go to be with girl at home

parts.note: Jo is a girl's name
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: An invitation to go and keep a girl company where she lives.
explanation.definitionFit: To join someone is to go and be in their company, a phrase synonym.

clue.text: Scientist argues really well at first in row

indicators.note: in places those initials inside the word for row

parts.note: a din is a row, a loud noise

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: A scientist argues his case convincingly in a heated quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' here is a noise (DIN), not a quarrel; 'at first' gives ARW, which goes 'in' DIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Darwin was the naturalist who proposed evolution by natural selection, an example of a scientist.

clue.text: Flier's clothes keep in warmth

indicators.note: keep in means the clothes word holds the warmth word within it

parts.note: wear means clothes, as in evening wear
heat means warmth

explanation.surface: A bird's feathers serve as clothes that keep it warm.
explanation.definitionFit: The wheatear is a small migratory songbird, so an example of something that flies.

clue.text: Full meeting in place, menu to be worked out

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place in addresses

indicators.note: worked out suggests the letters of menu being rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A meeting is held in a venue where the menu needs deciding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be worked out' signals the anagram of MENU; PL is a standard address abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A plenum is an assembly attended by all members, so a full meeting.

clue.text: For the moment, time is nothing up north

parts.note: now means for the moment, at present

explanation.surface: A northerner says there is nothing happening just now.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowt is the Northern English dialect word for nothing.

clue.text: Perhaps consul's not finished off certificate

indicators.note: not finished off means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a consul is an example of a diplomat, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: A consul has not finished signing off a certificate.
explanation.definitionFit: A diploma is a certificate awarded for completing a course of study.

clue.text: Man will ring, and say this first?

parts.note: he is a man
'll is the contracted form of will
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A man promises to telephone, and wonders what to open with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' is a circle (O), though the surface makes it a phone call, which suits the greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Hello is the greeting you would say first on answering a phone or meeting someone.

clue.text: Cocktail ingredient right for man to swallow

indicators.note: to swallow means the piece takes the right letter inside it

parts.note: a pawn is a chess man, a piece

explanation.surface: A man downs a drink made for him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cocktail' is the prawn cocktail starter, not a drink; 'man' is a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Prawns are the main ingredient of a prawn cocktail, a classic British starter.

clue.text: Shelved piece of furniture that now needs replacing

indicators.note: replacing means the letters of that now are put into new places

explanation.surface: An old shelving unit is due to be swapped for a new one.
explanation.definitionFit: A whatnot is a stand with open shelves for displaying ornaments, an antique furniture piece.

clue.text: Lack of guile one never has to prove in court

definitions.meaning: ... as naivety, being free of cunning

definitions.text: one never has to prove in court
definitions.meaning: ... as not being guilty, presumed so the defence need not prove it

explanation.walkthrough: Under the presumption of innocence the prosecution must prove guilt; the accused never has to prove they are innocent.
explanation.definitionFit: Innocence means both guilelessness and freedom from legal guilt, two senses of one word.

clue.text: In court, unscrupulous type gets years

parts.note: a chancer is an opportunist who takes unscrupulous risks

explanation.surface: A con artist is sentenced to years in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Chancery is a division of the English High Court, historically the Lord Chancellor's court.

clue.text: Damage marrow, destroying half

indicators.note: destroying half means only the first half of the word marrow survives

explanation.surface: Someone vandalises a prize vegetable, wrecking half of it.
explanation.walkthrough: A marrow is a large British garden vegetable like an overgrown courgette.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar something is to spoil or impair it, a synonym of damage.

clue.text: International organisation looking embarrassed and angry

parts.note: red-faced, so red means embarrassed
cross means angry

explanation.surface: A world body is described as both flustered and furious.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Cross is the worldwide humanitarian movement, an example of an international organisation.

clue.text: It's funny, whichever way you look at it

indicators.text: whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: whichever way you look at it says the answer reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: a joke, something funny

explanation.surface: Something is amusing from every angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whichever way you look at it' points to a word that is the same read from either end.
explanation.definitionFit: A gag is a joke, something meant to be funny.

clue.text: It's awkward being left in Calais

definitions.meaning: the French word for left, Calais being a French port

explanation.surface: It is uncomfortable to be abandoned in Calais.
explanation.definitionFit: Gauche means tactless or clumsy in English and simply left in French.

clue.text: A character man spared collapses

indicators.note: collapses suggests the words falling apart and their letters reforming

explanation.surface: A man who was spared then falls down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay; all nine letters of MAN SPARED are the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampersand is the typographic symbol &, a character meaning and.

clue.text: Leaving car briefly for teatime snack

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: parking is leaving a car somewhere

explanation.surface: Someone stops the car for a quick bite at teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: Parkin is a sticky ginger and oatmeal cake from Northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Parkin is a cake traditionally eaten with tea, so a teatime snack.

clue.text: A couple in old vessel, busy

indicators.note: in places the number inside the vessel word

parts.note: Noah's ark is the old vessel
a couple is two

explanation.surface: Two by two the animals board the ark, kept busy.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's 'A' is part of 'A couple', not a separate letter; 'in' places the number inside Noah's boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at work is to be occupied with a task, so busy.

clue.text: Doorman that's aimed at the head

definitions.meaning: a ... guards the door of a club
in cricket a ... is a short ball that rises towards the batsman's head

explanation.definitionFit: Bouncer names both a club's door security man and a short-pitched cricket delivery.

clue.text: Loudly disapprove of new benefit

parts.note: to boo is to jeer loudly

explanation.surface: People jeer a newly introduced welfare payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A boon is a blessing or advantage, a synonym of benefit.

clue.text: Its blades cut blades

parts.note: a machine with cutting blades used on blades of grass

explanation.surface: A tool whose sharp edges slice through other blades.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'blades' are blades of grass.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawn machine has rotating blades that cut grass, the blades of a lawn.

clue.text: Object to wits

explanation.definitionFit: Mind as a verb means to dislike or object, and as a noun means intellect.

clue.text: Different part of bible seen by woman

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, part of the Bible
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A woman reads a passage of scripture that seems unfamiliar.
explanation.definitionFit: Other means distinct or not the same, a synonym of different.

clue.text: Pays no attention to singer, worried about nothing

indicators.note: about means going round, so the jumbled letters surround the zero
worried suggests the letters of singer being shaken up

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone snubs a vocalist who frets over trifles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' makes IGNRES from SINGER; 'about' puts it round O.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore someone is to disregard them, which is paying them no attention.
